title: Execute the completion/splitting pass as a lockstep rule and prove nested owned-bank lifetimes (no new kappa)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Matarener"} -->
_Requested by **Mark**_

## Change and mathematical scope

**Before:** the retained `compiler` premise prescribes zxv's chronological product, paid completion of small targets and disjoint splitting (p7-TENSOR.md, higher-moment-strictification) and then Sussman's lockstep flow; the completion/splitting step exists only as moment arithmetic, and `FINITE-PRECOMPILATION.md` §6 allocates one owned-centre bank per compiled unit instance, noting that "a smaller reuse allocation requires its own lifetime proof".

**After:** `research/lockstep-completion-pass` executes the pass and proves the lifetime statement. Status: two written lemmas with event-level corroboration; no new κ, no selected-record change.
- **Lemma A.** Completion to the floor `L` on each small target's own owner, then splitting of every paid job at the cutoff `J`, is a transformation `U -> U'` of finite native units. `U'` satisfies the lockstep hierarchy; its compiled programs pass the ownership invariants I1–I6 of our #4691 executor; every added job is a whole job on a field its unit owns; the rank-one surplus is preserved exactly; the net-tax identity (1) of `net-tax-rank-compiler` holds; the added records (pieces, completions, normalizer pairs, block relocations) have a closed per-unit count that the executor reproduces.
- **Lemma B.** Owned-bank lifetimes in the lockstep schedule are properly nested (the live units are the classes on the current path plus the nested programs), so a LIFO stack of bank slots suffices; its peak is an explicit recursion. The executor runs the stack allocator with a new invariant I7 and its measured peak equals the recursion on every case. The owned-field inventory `O` in `Z = W + O` can be the peak instead of the instance count.

Remaining obligations: the native content of completion jobs and normalizers, the all-column lift, the strict moment inequality, precision and analytic recovery are inherited. The physical half of `native_all_columns` (tape execution of `g^{⊗f}` at the retained tariff, see #5442) is not addressed; this package supplies exact record counts for that bill, not prices.

## Task and overlap

Base: canonical main `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`; package commit `38097c7f1`. Inputs pinned in SOURCES.json: `FINITE-PRECOMPILATION.md`, `p7-TENSOR.md`, `higher-moment-strictification/README.md`, `net-tax-rank-compiler/PROOF.md`, the #5413 `invoice.json`/`funding.json`, `FINITE-DAG-AUDIT.json`, and our `lockstep-live-role-audit/live_roles.py`. Object: the completion/splitting pass and the lockstep flow on the p7 and selected #5413 profiles (cutoffs `c=10,b=15` and `c=20,b=21`), tensor powers 1..3 at histogram level, one generation for compiled counts.

Task card `selected-stock-envelope`, scope **refined** (TASK.json): it continues #4691 (same card) toward the `compiler`/`owned_erasure` premises named in target 10 of #5428. Nearest work: #4691 (executor, separated rules only), #4832 (sharp split charge; moment arithmetic only), #4586/#4638 (chronological batch widths), #5364/#5404 (continuation tapes), #4192 (Beneš arena scan), #5442 (algebraic half of `native_all_columns`). None executes the pass or proves bank lifetimes.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/lockstep-completion-pass
```

PASS locally on CPython 3.12 (Windows), standard library only: verify 148 s, controls 168 s; `check_research_commit.py` passes. Evidence:
- counting parity with #4691 on the toy rule (N = 4..64) and the BIT-shaped rule (N = 50..3200), and the FINITE-DAG-AUDIT receipt at toy rank 40;
- complete p7 and selected profiles at tensor powers 1, 2, 3: identity (1) to 40 digits, surplus unchanged (608 and 752 to the power v), equal added masses, separation; at v = 1 the selected unit has 77,204 rounds after the pass (64,260 original, 5,152 pieces, 7,792 completions), 15,584 normalizer records and 12,944 relocations;
- event-level execution with the stack allocator on the toy rule (full width to N = 28), an overlapping toy rule after the pass (full width, N = 40 and 64: 12,048 and 112,738 bank allocations, peaks 732 and 8,751), p7-shaped and selected-shaped rules with the caller's chronology shape and random, all-on-centre and one-owner owners: peak, total and all record counts equal the formulas;
- compiled counts of the complete profiles at one generation: selected profile N = 3045, 84,996 units per copy, 7,793 live at peak, total/peak banks = 346;
- twelve rejecting controls (`test_verify.py`): overlapping rule before the pass, cutoff not below floor, dropped remainder, short completion, foreign completion owner, release-early allocator, per-depth bank, eager parent, repeated exit field, peak recursion without its nested term, wrong tax, tampered RESULT.json.

Finite executions corroborate the written lemmas; they are not the all-size proof. Not run: the literal owner of each selected paid call (shaped chronologies instead), two-generation compiled counts for the selected profile, the v = 1024 template, Lean, hosted CI before this PR.

Apache-2.0. Prepared by Mark (Matarener) with substantial Claude Code assistance; no independent human or formal-kernel review.

## Open next questions

1. Bind the actual owners of the selected caller's paid calls and execute the literal 77,204-round rule at two lockstep copies (first step: per-event owner fields from `NEUTRAL-BACKWARD-v16c.json`).
2. Price the added records with the retained native tariff (171-record monomial bound, block-permutation price) for a numeric movement bill.
3. Evaluate `peak(N)`/`total(N)` at two generations with memoisation over dilations.
